title: Minimal VDOM Diff & Patch Engine
subtopicTitle: Critical Rendering Path: Reflow vs Repaint
concept: Virtual DOM Reconciliation & Minimal Mutation Operations
problemStatement: Implement `diff(oldVNode, newVNode)` that returns a list of patch instructions (`{ type: 'REPLACE'|'TEXT'|'PROPS', ... }`) to update `oldVNode` into `newVNode` with minimal operations.
interviewTrap: Assuming that tag changes can be patched in place. If tags differ (`div` -> `span`), the entire node must be replaced.

testCases.name: Generates REPLACE patch when tag changes
testCases.testFn: const p = diff({ tag: 'div', props: {} }, { tag: 'span', props: {} }); return p[0].type;

testCases.name: Generates PROPS patch when attributes change
testCases.testFn: const p = diff({ tag: 'div', props: { className: 'old' } }, { tag: 'div', props: { className: 'active' } }); return p[0].props;

testCases.name: Returns empty patches when nodes are identical
testCases.testFn: const p = diff({ tag: 'div', props: { id: 'x' } }, { tag: 'div', props: { id: 'x' } }); return p.length;

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Reflow recalculates geometry and layout tree (expensive). Repaint redraws pixels without changing geometry. Composite occurs on the GPU (transforms and opacity). Reading layout properties (`offsetWidth`, `scrollTop`) right after writing them forces synchronous layout thrashing.
